sounds.intro: Old English spelling was close to phonetic, and scholars reconstruct its sounds from the values of the Latin alphabet, from the alliteration of verse and from the regular changes that led to Middle and Modern English. This guide follows the late West Saxon pronunciation of around 1000 described in Mitchell and Robinson's Guide to Old English. The consonants and simple vowels are fairly secure. The exact sound of the diphthongs is not.

tips.p: Stress the first syllable of the root: CY-ning, HLĀ-ford, HEO-fon. Verb prefixes such as ge-, be-, for-, on- and ā- are never stressed (ge-BRÆC, on-LĒAC). Nouns often stress theirs, as in AND-swaru 'answer'.
Every letter is said. Final -e is a light vowel (heorte has two syllables), c and n are both heard in cniht, and w and r in wrecan.
Vowel length changes meaning: God 'God' but gōd 'good', is 'is' but īs 'ice'. Scribes almost never marked it. Macrons are a modern editor's aid.
Whether c and g soften depends on the vowels around them in prehistoric English, not on the spelling you see, so learn the sound with the word. This course does not print the dots some textbooks use.
The course spells words in normalised early West Saxon, as many textbooks do. The sounds here are the later West Saxon of Ælfric's time, when ie had become i or y.

grammar.title: Present tense
grammar.note: Weak lufian keeps its vowel. Strong verbs take -e, -st, -þ in the singular and change their vowel only in the past.

grammar.title: Weak nouns
grammar.note: Weak nouns end in -an everywhere except the nominative singular and the neuter accusative singular. eorþe goes like sunne: on eorþan.

sunne 'sun' (f)

grammar.title: Past tense
grammar.note: Weak verbs add -de or -ode. Strong verbs change their vowel, often to a different one in the plural.

singan 'sing'

grammar.title: Alliteration in the half-line
grammar.note: The first stress of the second half sets the sound. One or both stresses of the first half match it, and the last stress does not. Any vowel alliterates with any other.
